claims.text: A liquid-phase precursor route with optimized atmosphere control will produce single-phase ZrB2 at 1800–2000 °C.
The proposed route will produce dense ZrB2 at 1800–2000 °C.
Complete removal of organic byproducts depends on optimized atmosphere control.
ZrB2 made by the proposed route will have lower porosity than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
ZrB2 made by the proposed route will resist defect formation during prolonged liquid-plating-bath exposure better than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
The liquid-phase precursor forms a nanoscale precursor network.
Thermal decomposition of the precursor network produces uniformly nucleated ZrB2.
Uniform nucleation produces a dense ZrB2 phase with minimal residual porosity.
Enhanced atomic mixing in the precursor reduces diffusion distances.
Reduced diffusion distances enable near-complete ZrB2 crystallization at lower temperatures.
Optimized atmosphere control prevents contamination by organic residues.
Preventing contamination by organic residues promotes a defect-free microstructure.
A defect-free microstructure minimizes pore initiation during corrosive liquid-plating exposure.
Conventional preparation of single-phase ZrB2 uses temperatures above 2300 °C.
Conventionally prepared high-temperature ZrB2 typically has higher porosity than material made by the proposed route.
Conventionally prepared high-temperature ZrB2 is prone to defect formation during prolonged liquid-plating exposure.
Improved densification will lead to fewer surface defects and better structural integrity during long-term liquid-plating exposure.
The optimal atmosphere-control parameters for eliminating organic residue and preventing impurity incorporation remain undetermined.
